description: A three-panel composite figure of two modalities — one optical micrograph and two TEM bright-field images — documenting the κ-pearlite eutectoid constituent in a Fe-13.5Mn-6.3Al-0.78C steel after solution treatment at 1000 °C and aging at 600 °C for 100 h. (a) Optical micrograph, scale bar 100 µm: light, largely featureless matrix (austenite grains) outlined by dark, lacy, sometimes Widmanstätten-like colonies and grain-boundary allotriomorphs of κ-pearlite, with a few intragranular particles. (b) TEM bright-field image, scale bar 0.2 µm, of the interior of a κ-pearlite: alternating light α lamellae and dark lamellae labelled C, crossed in the lower half by a thick, straight band labelled κ, with a bent/dislocated band at the bottom. (c) TEM bright-field image, scale bar 0.2 µm, of a second colony interior with finer parallel lamellae labelled α (light), κ (dark) and short dark segments labelled C at the top edge and along the lamellae. The caption states C indicates M23C6. No numeric data values are printed; only scale bars. The panels together argue that the γ matrix decomposes eutectoidally into a lamellar α + κ + M23C6 mixture whose colony-scale arrangement is set by the austenite grain boundaries.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is an optical micrograph with a 100 µm scale bar in which dark, lacy colony-shaped features (κ-pearlite) decorate the boundaries of large light-appearing austenite grains.
Panels (b) and (c) are TEM bright-field images each carrying a 0.2 µm scale bar, i.e. roughly a 500× higher magnification than panel (a).
Lamellae inside the κ-pearlite colonies are individually labelled α (light), κ (dark) and C (short dark segments) in both TEM panels.
In panel (b) the κ band is markedly thicker/steeper than the adjacent alternating α and C lamellae, indicating κ is one of the coarser lamellar constituents of the eutectoid mixture.
No numeric data values (compositions, temperatures, spacings) are printed in any panel; the only quantitative markings are the scale bars.
The caption states the material is a Fe-13.5Mn-6.3Al-0.78C steel solution treated at 1000 °C and aged at 600 °C for 100 h.
The caption states that (a) shows large κ-pearlite colonies along the austenite grain boundaries, while (b) and (c) are TEM bright-field images revealing the internal portions of various κ-pearlites.
The caption states that the label 'C' in the TEM images indicates M23C6 carbide.
The citing text describes the lamellae as (α + κ + M23C6) formed by a eutectoid reaction, i.e. γ → α + κ + M23C6, during isothermal aging below 650 °C.

The citing text states that because the Al concentration is above the eutectoid composition, proeutectoid ferrite and κ-carbide form in the austenite before the eutectoid reaction, reducing the Al content of the retained austenite.
The citing text cites Lin et al. [132] for M23C6 complex carbide forming on γ/γ grain boundaries in a Fe-26.6Mn-8.8Al-0.61C alloy aged at 550 °C for 10–40 h.
Colony interiors in (b) and (c) show lamellae of distinctly different widths, suggesting the κ, α and C constituents are not uniformly spaced within a colony.

TEM bright-field image with a 0.2 µm scale bar: alternating light α and dark C lamellae crossed by a thick straight band labelled κ in the lower half; a bent, dislocated lamellar band runs along the bottom.
